description: Defines the biological background before the new perturbation is applied (cell model, genotype, disease, prior treatments). *Not* a claim to be falsified.
Direct physical binding of two biomolecules (drug-target, protein-protein, ligand-receptor).
signature: binds_to(id, actor, target, {affinity, unit, residues_actor, residues_target, via, confidence})

description: Increases or decreases the catalytic / signalling activity of a single protein, enzyme, transporter, TF or RNA.
Increases or decreases the activity of a named pathway or biological process (e.g. MAPK, autophagy, EMT).
Promotes assembly or causes disassembly of a multi-subunit complex; can include stoichiometry changes.
signature: modulates_complex(id, members, complex, direction, {stoichiometry, via, confidence})

description: Alters steady-state mRNA level or isoform ratio of one or more genes (bulk, single-cell or signature). Use `mechanism` to tag cases like alternative splicing.
signature: regulates_expression(id, regulator, gene_list, direction, {mechanism, via, confidence})

description: Post-transcriptional control at the ribosome level (e.g. eIF inhibition, uORF usage, IRES activation).
signature: regulates_translation(id, regulator, rna_id, direction, {mechanism, via, confidence})

description: Adds or removes a specific PTM or proteolytic cleavage on a protein site (phospho, ubiquitin, acetyl, etc.).
signature: post_translational_modification(id, protein, mod_type, site, direction, {via, confidence})

description: Moves a molecule between compartments. Use `to="extracellular"` for secretion or `from="extracellular"` for uptake; add `mechanism` (e.g. exocytosis, transporter).
signature: localises_to(id, entity, from_loc, to_loc, {mechanism, via, confidence})

description: Enzymatic conversion of one chemical entity into another (metabolic reaction or proteolytic processing).
Changes protein abundance by altering half-life (ubiquitin-proteasome degradation, PROTAC, chaperone rescue).
Genetic variant or edit that increases the normal activity of the specified protein.
Genetic variant, knock-down or knock-out that reduces or abolishes activity of the specified protein.
Creates or worsens a measurable phenotype or cell-state transition. Optional `from_state` / `to_state` capture events like EMT or senescence.
signature: induces_phenotype(id, source, phenotype, {via, confidence, from_state, to_state})

description: Reverts or mitigates an abnormal phenotype back toward normal (rescue). Same optional state fields as above.
signature: alleviates_phenotype(id, actor, phenotype, {via, confidence, from_state, to_state})

description: Non-causal functional similarity (transcriptomic, phenotypic, structural) between two entities.
Statistical association without established causality (GWAS hit, literature co-mention, co-expression).
Links an entity to a GO term, pathway or compartment (background annotation).
Ligand-receptor signalling from one cell type to another plus the immediate downstream outcome.
signature: cell_cell_interaction(id, sender, receiver, ligand, receptor, outcome, {via, confidence})

description: Adds or removes histone/DNA marks at a defined genomic locus, affecting chromatin accessibility.
